rows.question: How do I change the address on my driving licence?

answer.answer: Apply online, which is free. You need your driving licence and must be a resident of Great Britain (Northern Ireland has a different process) and not banned from driving. You can keep driving while you wait for the new licence. Alternatively, apply by post: for a paper licence, send a completed form D1 (car/motorbike) or D2 (lorry/bus), your licence, original identity documents and a passport photo, with the correct postage. For a photocard licence, complete the 'changes' section of letter D741 and send it with the photocard to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1BN, with the correct postage. You must also update your V5C log book, vehicle tax Direct Debit (if used), and any V750/V778 personalised registration document. Failing to tell DVLA can incur a fine of up to £1,000.

rows.question: How much does it cost to renew my driving licence when I turn 70?

answer.answer: Free. There is no fee to renew your driving licence when you're 70 or over, whether you apply online or by post.

rows.question: How old do I have to be to apply for a provisional driving licence?

answer.answer: You must be at least 15 years and 9 months old to apply for a provisional driving licence.

rows.question: How much does it cost to replace a stolen driving licence?
How long do penalty points stay on my licence?

answer.answer: Most penalty points stay on your driving record for 4 years from the date of the offence. For reckless/dangerous driving (DD40, DD60, DD80) or offences that result in disqualification, the 4 years runs from the date of conviction. Some offences stay for 11 years instead, but the extracts don't list which ones.

rows.question: How much does the car theory test cost?

answer.answer: £23 for cars (the same for weekdays and evenings, weekends and bank holidays).

rows.question: How do I tell DVLA my car is off the road?

answer.answer: Register it as off the road (SORN) with DVLA: apply online if the vehicle is registered in your name (you'll need the 11-digit V5C log book number or the 16-digit reference from your vehicle tax reminder), or apply by post using form V890 sent to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1AR. You can also phone the DVLA vehicle service on 0300 123 4321 (24-hour service). Start when you're ready to take the vehicle off the road. You'll get a refund for any full months of remaining tax, and you cannot use the vehicle on the road until you tax it again.

rows.question: Can I get a refund on my vehicle tax if I sell my car?

answer.answer: Yes. Tell DVLA the vehicle has been sold or transferred to someone else, and you'll automatically get a refund for any full months of remaining vehicle tax. The refund is calculated from the date DVLA receives your information and is sent as a cheque to the name and address on the vehicle log book. You won't get refunds for credit card fees, the 5% direct debit surcharge, or the 10% surcharge on a single 6-month payment.

rows.question: Which vehicles are exempt from vehicle tax?

answer.answer: Vehicles exempt from vehicle tax include: vehicles (apart from ambulances) used by organisations providing transport for disabled people; vehicles used for agriculture, horticulture and forestry (including tractors, agricultural engines, light agricultural vehicles used off-road, and 'limited use' vehicles making journeys of no more than 1.5km on a public road between land used by the same person); and any steam-powered vehicle. Historic vehicles can also be made exempt if they are cars, vans, motorcycles or tricycles, by applying for the exemption. Exempt vehicles must still be taxed even though no payment is due.

rows.question: How do I check the MOT history of a car?

answer.answer: Use the GOV.UK 'Check MOT history' service and enter the vehicle's number plate (registration number). It shows past pass/fail results, the recorded mileage, and when the next MOT is due. For cars, results are available for tests done since 2005. If the test was in England, Scotland or Wales, you can also download current and previous MOT certificates and see where each test was done (this needs the 11-digit number from the V5C log book).

rows.question: How early can I get my MOT without losing my renewal date?

answer.answer: Up to a month (minus a day) before your MOT runs out, which keeps the same renewal date. For example, if your MOT runs out on 15 May, the earliest is 16 April.

rows.question: What do I need to do when I sell my car?

answer.answer: Tell DVLA that you've sold the vehicle, using the online service, which changes the registered keeper and lets you send the log book (V5C) to the new keeper. Your vehicle tax will then be cancelled and you'll get a refund for any full months remaining. You can't use the service if you've already posted the log book or don't have it. If you don't have the log book, tell the buyer they'll need to fill in form V62 to apply for a V5C (£25 fee), and write to the DVLA Sensitive Casework Team in Swansea (SA99 1ZZ) with the sale date, the buyer's name and address, and who should receive any tax refund.

rows.question: How do I change the address on my V5C log book?

answer.answer: Online: use the DVLA online service (available Monday to Friday 7am to 9pm, and Saturday and Sunday 7am to 8pm). You must be the vehicle's registered keeper, and the new address must be a UK address. By post: for the new-style log book (multi-coloured numbered blocks on the front), write the new address in section 3 (no PO Box) and send the whole log book to the DVLA address in section 3. For the older-style log book, write the new address in section 6 (no PO Box), sign and send the whole log book to the DVLA address in section 8, and do not tick the 'new keeper' box or fill in your name. Pay the correct postage.

rows.question: What should I do if my car has been stolen?

answer.answer: Tell the police and your insurance company straight away. Call 101 and ask for your local police station, having your registration number, make and model, and colour ready; you'll get a crime reference number, which you need when you call your insurance company. Your insurance company will tell you how to make a claim. If it pays out, you must tell DVLA the vehicle has been sold to the insurance company.

rows.question: What are the penalties for speeding?

answer.answer: The minimum penalty for speeding is a £100 fine and 3 penalty points added to your licence. You could be disqualified from driving if you build up 12 or more penalty points within 3 years. If you plead not guilty and the court finds you guilty, you can be fined more (usually a percentage of your weekly income, up to £1,000, or £2,500 if on a motorway), get more penalty points, be disqualified or have your licence suspended. You may instead be offered a speed awareness course if the police consider it appropriate and you have not been on one in the past 3 years.

rows.question: How do I get my licence back after a driving ban?

answer.answer: Check your driving record online to see when the disqualification ends. Once it ends, you must apply for a new licence to drive again. If the court ordered you to retake your driving test, apply for a new provisional licence first, and you can drive once the ban is over and you have passed the tests you need.

rows.question: Can I drive if I have diabetes?

answer.answer: The extracts only cover when you must tell DVLA about diabetes (for example, insulin treatment lasting over 3 months or disabling hypoglycaemia). They do not say whether you can drive with diabetes in general.

rows.question: What are the eyesight rules for driving?

answer.answer: For driving generally: you must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres, with a visual acuity of at least decimal 0.5 (6/12) on the Snellen scale using both eyes together (or the one eye if you have sight in only one), wearing glasses or contact lenses if needed. You must also have an adequate field of vision, wear any needed glasses or lenses every time you drive, and tell DVLA about any eyesight problem affecting both eyes (or your remaining eye). Lorry and bus drivers must meet stricter standards: at least 0.8 (6/7.5) in the better eye and at least 0.1 (6/60) in the other, plus a horizontal visual field of at least 160 degrees.

rows.question: How do I change the photo on my driving licence?

answer.answer: You can renew your full or provisional driving licence to update the photo, which gives you a new licence. Online it costs £14 (you can use your passport photo or upload a new one; you must be a resident of Great Britain and not disqualified from driving). By post, get a 'D1 pack' from a Post Office that deals with DVLA photocard renewal, and send it with a recent printed passport-type photo, your current photocard and paper counterpart (or tick the box on the D1 form if lost), and a cheque or postal order for £17 payable to DVLA (no fee if over 70 or on a medical short period licence) to DVLA, Swansea SA99 1DH.

rows.question: What do the codes on my driving licence mean?

answer.answer: The codes on the back of your licence show the conditions you must meet to drive. For example, 01 means you need eyesight correction such as glasses or contact lenses, 78 means you may only drive vehicles with automatic transmission, and 101 means not for hire or reward. Some codes differ in Northern Ireland.

rows.question: How do I swap my paper driving licence for a photocard?

answer.answer: You only need to exchange a paper licence if you change your address or name, want Driver CPC training, or your licence is defaced, lost, stolen or destroyed. Otherwise a valid paper licence doesn't need exchanging. To exchange, you can sign in to renew online, unless you've changed your name, in which case you must apply by post using form D1 (cars and motorbikes) or D2 (buses and lorries), available from most Post Offices. Include original identity documents, a colour passport-type photo and the £20 fee if needed (cheques or postal orders payable to DVLA, no cash). Send cars and motorbikes applications to DVLA Swansea SA99 1BU, and buses and lorries to DVLA Swansea SA99 1BR.

rows.question: How much does the driving test cost?

answer.answer: For a car, the driving test costs £62 on weekdays and £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays.

rows.question: How do I change my driving test appointment?

answer.answer: Change it yourself online (your driving instructor cannot change it for you). The online service is available from 6am to 11:40pm. You'll need at least 2 of: your UK driving licence number, theory test pass certificate number, or driving test booking reference. You can make only 2 changes to your booking, and a change can be to the date or time, the test centre, or a swap. Northern Ireland uses a different service.

rows.question: How do I tax a car if I haven't received a tax reminder?

answer.answer: You can tax your vehicle without a reminder letter (V11), email or text by using a V5C logbook in your name (if you're the current keeper), a V62 application for a registration certificate (if you're the current keeper), or the green 'new keeper' slip (if you've just bought the car and don't yet have a V5C in your name). Online, you need the 11-digit reference number from your V5C, or the 12-digit reference number from the new keeper slip. You can also apply at a Post Office that deals with vehicle tax, where you may also need payment and evidence of a current MOT.

rows.question: I've just bought a used car. What do I need to do to tax it and get it registered in my name?

answer.answer: Tax the car immediately before using it on the road, using the green 'new keeper' slip from the log book (V5C) as your reference. The seller will usually register the vehicle in your name, online or by post. If the car has no V5C log book, you must register it yourself. You can tax online or at a Post Office that deals with vehicle tax, and you may need evidence of a valid MOT.

rows.question: I'm moving house. Which of my licence and vehicle records do I need to update?

answer.answer: Update the address on your driving licence and your vehicle log book (V5C). If you pay vehicle tax by Direct Debit, update that too. If you have a personalised registration number document (V750 or V778), update its address as well. You can be fined up to £1,000 if you do not tell DVLA when your address changes. Updating your licence address is free and you can still drive while waiting for the new licence.

rows.question: My car is over 40 years old. Does it need an MOT, and does it need vehicle tax?

answer.answer: No MOT is needed if the car was built or first registered more than 40 years ago and no 'substantial changes' (such as replacing the chassis, body, axles or engine) have been made. Vehicle tax: if the car was built before 1 January 1986, you can stop paying from 1 April 2026, but you must apply for a vehicle tax exemption (the 'historic tax class'). If you don't know the build date but it was registered before 8 January 1986, you don't need to pay from 1 April 2026. Even without an MOT, the car must stay roadworthy; using it in a dangerous condition can bring a fine of up to £2,500 and 3 penalty points.

rows.question: I'm 17 and want to learn to drive. What licence and tests do I need, and what do they cost?

answer.answer: Apply online for a first provisional driving licence for a car, which costs £34. You must be at least 15 years and 9 months old, able to read a number plate from 20 metres, and have been given permission to live in Great Britain for at least 185 days. You must also have lived in England, Wales or Scotland for at least 185 days in the 12 months before your theory or driving test. The car theory test costs £23. The driving test costs £62 on weekdays, or £75 on evenings, weekends and bank holidays.

rows.question: My car has been written off. What do I tell DVLA and what happens to my vehicle tax?

answer.answer: Tell DVLA that your vehicle has been written off (you can be fined £1,000 if you don't). Once DVLA receives this, you'll be sent a letter confirming you're no longer the keeper, and a vehicle tax refund for any full months left. If you pay vehicle tax by Direct Debit, it's cancelled automatically.

rows.question: I'm over 70 and have a medical condition. How do I renew my driving licence?

answer.answer: Renew online at the GOV.UK service if you're 70 or over (or will be within 90 days), you're a resident of Great Britain, you meet the minimum eyesight requirement, and you're not prevented from driving for any reason. You'll need to sign in, and you must declare any notifiable medical condition on the application form; you don't need to contact DVLA separately. Licences are renewed every 3 years once you reach 70. If you hold a C1 or D1 entitlement, you must renew by post.

rows.question: Which car insurance company is cheapest for a new driver?

answer.answer: The extracts do not name or compare any insurance companies or their prices, so they cannot say which is cheapest for a new driver.

rows.question: How do I renew my driving licence in Northern Ireland?

answer.answer: Apply to the Driver and Vehicle Agency (DVA). The GOV.UK pages say the online renewal service is for Great Britain residents only, and Northern Ireland has a different service run by the DVA.

rows.question: Will my appeal against a speeding fine succeed?

answer.answer: The extracts do not say whether an appeal against a speeding fine will succeed. They only describe the penalties for pleading guilty or not guilty, and what happens at court if you plead not guilty.

rows.question: How much income tax will I pay on a company car?

answer.answer: The extracts cover vehicle tax (Vehicle Excise Duty) only and do not mention income tax or company car benefit-in-kind taxation.

rows.question: Can you recommend a good driving instructor near me?

answer.answer: The extracts do not name or recommend specific driving instructors. They only say you can find your nearest driving instructors on GOV.UK, and that instructors must be a qualified driving instructor (ADI) or trainee and display a green or pink badge.

rows.question: How many times can I change my car driving test booking now?

answer.answer: You can make 2 changes to a car driving test booking. Changing the date or time, or the test centre, counts as one change, even if you change both at once. Other test types (not car tests) still allow 6 changes.

rows.question: Can my driving instructor book or cancel my driving test for me?

answer.answer: No. You must book and cancel your car driving test yourself. Your driving instructor is not allowed to book or cancel it for you, and it's against the law to book a car driving test for someone else.

rows.question: If I want to move my driving test to a different test centre, where can I move it to?

answer.answer: You can move your test to any of the 3 test centres nearest to where your test is currently booked, or back to the test centre you first booked at on that current booking. If you booked before 9 June 2026, the nearest-centres rule applies to the centre your test was booked at on 9 June 2026, not where you first booked.

rows.question: The mileage on my MOT record is wrong. How do I get it corrected?

answer.answer: Use the online form at GOV.UK to report the mistake. If the MOT was more than 28 days ago, you can report the mileage through the form. If it was in the last 28 days, the form will tell you how to report it. You must upload a document showing the correct mileage at the time of the MOT: an invoice, emissions printout, service receipt, vehicle service history, or a job card or inspection sheet from the MOT centre. The document must show the registration number or VIN, the mileage, and a date within one day of the MOT test. An MOT certificate or a photo of the dashboard cannot be used. You'll usually get a reply within 8 weeks. If the MOT was in Northern Ireland, contact the DVA instead.

rows.question: How do I set up a Direct Debit to pay my vehicle tax?

answer.answer: You can set up a Direct Debit when you tax your vehicle online or at a Post Office. You need your address and date of birth, and your bank or building society name, account number and sort code. You cannot use an account that needs 2 signatures. You do not need to be the registered keeper to set it up. You'll get a confirmation by email or post; the first payment is taken once the vehicle tax has started (can take up to 10 days), and later payments are taken on the first working day of the month the Direct Debit is due.
